paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and shear property of high-temperature brazing of TiAl alloy and 316L stainless steel with a Ni-based amorphous filler

evidence.quote: TiAl alloy is a new type of superalloy material with superior comprehensive properties, such as high specific strength, specific stiffness, creep resistance, oxidation resistance and low density
Stainless steel has low cost, strong corrosion resistance, easy processing, etc.

a high-melting-point Ni-based amorphous ribbon with a nominal composition of Ni60Nb15Zr15Ti10 was fabricated by utilizing electron beam melting and single roll spin quenching technology and applied as the filler metal to braze TiAl alloy and 316L stainless steel.

The adjacent irregular block phases marked with B may be determined to be AlNi2Ti.

phases_and_microstructures.name: cleavage step
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: brazed at 1090 °C, tested at room temperature and 750 °C

evidence.quote: The high-density short and curved cleavage steps could be found from the figure of both fracture surfaces, which is characteristic of quasi-cleavage fracture.

phases_and_microstructures.name: secondary crack
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: brazed at 1090 °C, tested at room temperature and 750 °C

evidence.quote: there is also a small fracture around the cleavage steps, the fracture surface is perpendicular to the shear stress, the fracture is flush and bright, and secondary cracks can be found, which indicates the high brittleness of the joint.
